findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The split at line 964 treats an abbreviation as a sentence ending: `Dr. Smith cannot sign in. Reset the session.` produces `Dr`. It also misses a sentence ending in a curly closing quote: `The command prints “Failed.” Retry it.` retains both sentences. The named command test covers a straight closing quote, but neither of these cases.

findings.body:
Gain 1, Work 1, Harm 1
The proof list claims shortened titles have no trailing punctuation, but the long-why cases in this test and `test_1_fix_title_is_the_whole_first_sentence` cut after an ordinary word. They would still pass if the punctuation removal on close.py line 967 were removed. A why with a comma immediately before the shortening boundary exercises the claimed behavior.
